picks.title: CMA takes first steps to ensure choice in business software (proposes Microsoft strategic market status, AI tools in scope)
picks.excerpt: Primary doc: the UK Competition and Markets Authority proposes designating Microsoft with strategic market status in business software, explicitly citing agentic AI in workplace tools and whether rival AI providers get a level playing field.
picks.rationale: Primary document and a new regulatory decision: the CMA's proposed strategic-market-status designation explicitly puts agentic AI in workplace software and rival AI providers' access in scope, which directly affects anyone building AI tools on top of Microsoft's stack. Copy must say the designation is proposed, not final. The og_image is a generic GOV.UK card, so ax-media should source an in-article image.

picks.title: Western open-weight models still can't beat China
picks.excerpt: Chinese open-weight AI models offer high capability at far lower cost than US frontier systems but face monetization and compute constraints, experts said at a Rest of World event.
picks.rationale: Replaces the UK UN First Committee statement, in which AI turned out to be incidental. This is the remaining geopolitics-axis item: expert assessment of how the US and China compare on open-weight models, covering cost and capability gaps and Chinese compute and monetization limits. It is a different piece from the 10-08 Axios card about new Western releases. Attribute every assessment to the named panelists and present it as an event discussion, not as news of a release.

picks.title: Commission launches RAISE pledging initiative to boost AI support for researchers across Europe
picks.excerpt: Primary doc: at the European AI in Science Summit in Dublin the Commission launched the RAISE (Resource for AI Science in Europe) pledging initiative for AI-in-science enablers.
picks.rationale: A formal new Commission programme (the RAISE pledging initiative) for compute, data and support for AI in science, released as an official press release. It is distinct from the 10-12 Tech Policy Press summit-atmosphere card. Describe what pledgers commit to and who can join. The og_image is the EC logo, so source an in-article image.

picks.title: The EU is facing Big Tech pressure to revamp its AI law
picks.excerpt: Microsoft and Google DeepMind executives are pushing Brussels to rework the AI Act for the newest frontier models; Commission officials insist the law is strong enough to handle their security risks.
picks.rationale: First report of Microsoft and Google DeepMind formally pressing the Commission to rework the AI Act for frontier models, with the Commission's on-record answer that the law is enough. This bears on AI Act obligations for model builders. Present both positions and attribute each to the party that holds it.

picks.title: How are countries evaluating AI models?
picks.excerpt: Brookings background briefing (for the FCAI dialogue) comparing how governments and AI safety institutes test and evaluate frontier AI models.
picks.rationale: A newly published comparative briefing on how national governments and AI safety institutes test frontier models. It is not an op-ed, and it gives builders a practical map of the evaluation regimes their models may face. Present it as a Brookings briefing, not as a government decision.

alternates.title: EU's cyber unit turns to AI to fend off 'high-risk' hacks
alternates.excerpt: The European Commission's IT department wants to deploy AI to defend its systems against the most serious cyberattacks.
alternates.rationale: Weak backup: a minor internal procurement plan. Its nearest published story is https://www.gov.uk/government/news/britain-steps-up-national-defences-against-growing-ai-risks (related only).
